# The Zimmermann UI build pattern — extracted from PR #56 and PR #59

---

## Part 1 — PR #56: `refactor(theme): zimmTokens single source of truth + var(--zimm-*) consistency`

**Merged** 2026-08-18 · branch `feature/theme-token-consistency` · 17 files, +705/−462 · author `TimLavelleACC`

### 1a. Body and review conversation

The body frames five concerns, each a *drift-closure* argument rather than a feature:

1. `zimmTokens.ts` "made fully derived" from `colour.ts`/`spacing.ts`/`typography.ts`/`sizes.ts` "instead of hand-retyped literals, closing a drift risk that previously had only a Vitest test as a safety net."
2. `button.ts` established as "the single source of truth for button styling" — `globalStyles.ts`'s parallel `.zimm-btn-*` class system deleted outright because it had "real value conflicts (different heights, transparent-vs-opaque secondary background, zero interactive states)."
3. `header.ts`/`listMenu.ts` brought onto `var(--zimm-*)`; untokenised values "flagged with a comment rather than silently retimed."
4. New `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` (178 lines, net-new) documenting the resulting hierarchy.
5. px → rem conversion for WCAG 1.4.4, px retained only for hairline geometry.

The body also names the *deliberate scope-down*: `link.ts` excluded because "the component doesn't exist on `develop` yet — separate PR", plus `f2r/`, CI work, demo deletions, and a cosmetic formatting diff. And: "All referenced `var(--zimm-*)` tokens were confirmed to already exist on `develop`'s `zimmTokens.ts` before branching."

**Review conversation.** Three PR-level comments, nine reviews. The Protected File Guard bot posted the Tier 2 notice for `navConstants.ts`, `button.ts`, `header.ts`, `listMenu.ts`. CodeRabbit produced exactly **one actionable inline nitpick** and **two `vendor.d.ts` findings**:

- *Nitpick, fixed*: "Centralise the unresolved navigation letter-spacing value. Both files hardcode the same prototype value." → resolved by creating `overrides/app/theme/components/navConstants.ts` (5 lines) holding `NAV_LETTER_SPACING`, imported by both. Commit `4fce726`.
- *Two `vendor.d.ts` findings, declined with a written rationale on-thread*. The author's reply is the template for how declines are done here — it names the reason, the rule, and the follow-up:

  > "Not acting on either: the `Link`/`NavLink`/`useParams` ambient types were added ahead of the Link component override … that component is deliberately excluded from this PR … Adding `@types/react-router-dom` is a new devDependency, which per this repo's AGENTS.md Hard Rule 7 needs integration-team approval — out of scope for this PR to just add. Will revisit … in the Link-component follow-up PR, scoped to whatever props that component actually uses."

- One finding *was* fixed rather than deferred (the loose ambient types with `state: any`), and the body says so explicitly: "a CodeRabbit finding on this PR's own diff, fixed rather than deferred."

### 1b. File-level diff shape, grouped by concern

| Concern | Files |
|---|---|
| Token derivation | `foundation/zimmTokens.ts` (+133/−118), `colour.ts` (+83/−70), `typography.ts` (+123/−89), `spacing.ts` (+25/−13), `sizes.ts` (+4/−3), `foundation/index.ts` (+2/−2) |
| Single-surface enforcement | `theme/globalStyles.ts` (+6/−88 — the `.zimm-btn-*` deletion), `theme/components/button.ts` (+35/−38) |
| Convention alignment | `theme/components/header.ts`, `listMenu.ts`, new `navConstants.ts` |
| Regression net | `theme/index.test.tsx` (+27/−12) |
| Governance / docs | `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` (new, +178), `.docs/memory/projectState.md`, `.claude/registry/components.md`, `coderabbit.yaml` |
| Incidental typing fix | `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts` (+43/−3) |

### 1c. Commit sequence

```
1  63dfe00  refactor(theme): apply zimmTokens single-source convention to header, listMenu
2  2381909  chore(coderabbit): exclude f2r/ from AI review scope
3  5b36062  refactor(theme): make zimmTokens.ts fully derived, button.ts the single source of truth
4  4fce726  fix(theme): address CodeRabbit findings on PR #56
5  e1732a3  Merge branch 'develop' into feature/theme-token-consistency
```

What the order reveals: **the convention is applied to an existing consumer first (1), before the source of truth is restructured (3).** Commit 1 proves the `var(--zimm-*)` convention works against real recipes; only then does commit 3 rewrite `zimmTokens.ts` to be derived and delete the competing class system. Commit 4 is a single dedicated review-response commit, not amendments folded back. Every commit body carries a *why*, and commit 2's body records the Tier 1 identity verification inline:

> "Tier 1 file (coderabbit.yaml) — verified via `gh api` that the authenticated identity (TimLavelleACC) is a member of @ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers before making this change, per AGENTS.md's Tier 1 Approval verified-session exception."

## Part 2 — PR #59: `feat(footer): SFCC-55 global footer UI`

**Merged** 2026-08-24 · branch `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui` · merge commit `8362b3c` · 132 files, +8724/−1187

### 2a. Body

The body is structured to *pre-empt review friction*. Sections: Description → three "points worth surfacing before review" → Linked (ticket, Figma node, sign-off names + date, test-case IDs) → Squad ownership → Types of Changes → Changes (grouped by concern with the rationale inline) → How to test-drive → **Protection-tier check** → Testing checklist.

Two paragraphs from "Changes" carry the load-bearing architectural decisions:

> "`theme/components/footer.ts` — the `ZimmFooter` multipart recipe. Named `ZimmFooter`, not `Footer`: `extendTheme` deep-merges, so a recipe sharing a base SFCC recipe's name inherits it rather than replacing it"

> "`components/ui-kits/` — six atoms/molecules; `cssVars` indirection removed in favour of the `--zimm-*` custom properties directly, and `utils/cssVars.ts` deleted"

The Protection-tier check block names each protected path, its tier, its owner, and the authorisation basis — including "Authenticated as `marcelannavarro`, a member of `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`." The Testing block is 9 checked lines with counts (`168/168`, `15 play functions across 7 stories`, `112 footer elements × 6 viewports, 0 off-token paddings`, `axe 0 violations / 17 passes`).

The body also **flags pre-existing defects it is not fixing** (`header/index.tsx`'s `fontSize="l"` and `useCurrentBasket`) and **flags mechanical noise** ("9 of the 16 new commits carry `.claude/registry/` churn … Mechanical — skip those hunks").

### 2b. Review conversation

- **179 inline comments** across **57 top-level threads**: 118 from `coderabbitai[bot]`, 61 replies from `marcelannavarro`. Plus 17 PR-level comments and 136 review submissions.
- Two auto-bots fire first: the Protected File Guard (Tier 2 notice listing all 17 shared files including every `.css.ts`) and the MRT preview-environment deploy.
- CodeRabbit auto-paused reviews ("branch under active development"); the author drove it manually with `@coderabbitai review` / `full-review` / `resolve`.

**How findings were resolved.** Every thread got an in-thread reply — this is mandated by AGENTS.md ("A fix commit alone, with no reply posted on the thread, doesn't count"). Three resolution modes:

*Fixed, with the mechanism explained and blast radius stated:*
> "Fixed in `706e47d`. Rather than adding a component-level JSDoc, `extractDescription` now takes the row's own declaration name … Demoting the offending comment was tried first and just handed the row to the next JSDoc down (`NEW_TAB_SUFFIX`) … Blast radius checked before committing: only 2 registry rows moved."

*Fixed, with the finding generalised beyond what was asked:*
> "Fixed in `fce5af1`. `heading === 'Contact'` is gone; the three sites now key off a `showContactChannels` boolean on the group. Verified locale-independent by renaming the fixture heading to `Kontakt` … `CONTACT_GROUP_HEADING` was removed entirely so the string cannot come back."

*Deferred with acceptance criteria, or declined with the rule cited.* The author posted a public round-up comment (2026-08-21T17:23) that reads as the canonical form:
> "**Deferred to HPC-035** with your acceptance criteria noted on the thread: the focus-containment branch in `useSubscribeModal` … Both unreachable while `enableNameCapture` defaults to false. **Deferred to HPC-034:** production values for `phoneHref`, `whatsAppHref` and `emailHref` … **Declined with rationale on-thread:** the `.storybook/` and `foundation/fonts.ts` findings (verified tier-1-approver session per AGENTS.md's Tier 1 Approval section; both comment/config-only, no token changed), and the `header/index.tsx` `fontSize="l"` correction, which predates this branch by two months and belongs to an ast-grep rule rather than a footer PR."

CodeRabbit responded by writing two **persistent learnings** back into its model keyed to this PR. Notably the author also self-corrected mid-review:
> "You were right that this failed CI, and my own check missed it — I grepped case-sensitively for `\"Clear input\"` while the story matched `/clear input/i`."

The highest-value findings that changed the architecture: unsafe-href guard extracted to `overrides/app/utils/safeHref.ts` and shared between footer and `ZimmNavItem`; `showContactChannels` flag replacing English-string matching; `clearable` made opt-in; contact-channel fields added to both the Contentful schema *and* the TypeScript type together.

### 2c. File-level diff shape, grouped by concern

| Concern | Files |
|---|---|
| **Footer feature** | `footer/index.tsx` (+219), `footer/footer.css.ts` (+142), `footer/footerNavColumn/{index.tsx,footerNavColumn.css.ts,index.test.tsx}`, `footer/bottomBar/{index.tsx,bottomBar.css.ts}`, `footer/index.stories.tsx` (+262), `footer/index.stories.content.ts` (+144), `footer/index.test.tsx` (+221) |
| **ui-kit atoms** | `ui-kits/atoms/{zimmButton,zimmIcon,zimmLogo,zimmModal,zimmNavItem,zimmTextInput}/` — each `index.tsx` + `index.stories.tsx` (+ `<name>.css.ts` where it has one) |
| **ui-kit molecules** | `ui-kits/molecules/{zimmContactIconRow,zimmInputAction}/` |
| **ui-kit organisms** | `ui-kits/organisms/{zimmSubscribeModal,zimmSubscribeSection}/` |
| **Hooks (extracted state)** | `useSubscribeSection.ts`, `useZimmModal.ts`, `useZimmTextInputState.ts`, `useUiCopy.ts` — each with a `.test.ts(x)` |
| **Utils** | `utils/safeHref.ts` + test, `utils/resolveByRegion.ts` + test |
| **Theme** | `theme/components/index.ts` (+19/−1), `theme/components/footerShared.ts` (+28), `theme/components/button.ts` (**−119, deleted/moved**), `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` (+365), `theme/fontFace.tsx` + test |
| **Icons** | `components/icons/zimm.tsx` (+185 — the four chevrons), `icons/index.tsx` |
| **Contentful** | `scripts/contentful/content-types/{footerConfig,footerNavGroup,link,region,uiCopy}.js`, `buildTemplate.js`, `setup/installTemplate.mjs`, `setup/seedRegions.mjs`; deleted `sync.js`, `runMigrations.mjs`, `detectDrift.mjs`, `migrations/`; `types/contentful.ts` (+119) |
| **Tooling / governance** | `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` (**new, +167**), `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` (+266/−…), `CODEOWNERS`, `.claude/rules/{overrideStyling,css,components,testing,frozenFiles,protectedFiles}.md`, `.cursor/`, `.vscode/`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` |
| **Fonts** | `static/fonts/*.woff2`, `.storybook/{main.js,preview.tsx}` |

### 2d. Commit sequence — 45 commits

The full sequence is best read as **six phases**. Selected commits with what they reveal:

**Phase 1 — Scaffold (1–8).** `8c25f11 feat(footer): … atoms, molecules, subscribe modal, and Figma token alignment` builds everything inline in one commit. Then a run of `fix(ui-kit)`/`fix(footer)` commits absorbing the first CodeRabbit pass, plus Figma pixel corrections quoting node IDs: `f681d75 … Desktop site-map: flex:1 fill → flex:0 0 600px fixed (Figma node 40000407:11736 w-[600px])`.

**Phase 2 — Token indirection, then its reversal (9–14, 24, 28).** `a2a2af4 refactor(ui-kit): introduce cssVars utility` created `utils/cssVars.ts` exporting `var(--zimm-*)` strings as named constants. Fourteen commits later `78f2236` deletes it:
> "The cssVars object was an indirection over strings that are already the public contract … A recipe reading `cssVars.font.size['3xs']` and one reading `'var(--zimm-font-size-3xs)'` emit identical CSS, but the former hides which variable is in play at the point of use and needs a second lookup to review. Every consumer now names the variable directly, and `utils/cssVars.ts` is deleted rather than left orphaned."

**Phase 3 — Move styling into recipes (15, 18, 21, 29).**
- `dc86c13 refactor(ui-kit): migrate ZimmButton to Chakra Button+button.ts` — "so all interaction states (hover, press, focus, disabled) live in CSS pseudo-props, not React state … remove useState for hovered/pressed/focused".
- `3a37a4c refactor(footer): extract provisional values to _foundation, wire footer.ts theme config` — "connect via `useMultiStyleConfig` — `footer/index.tsx` now uses `chakra.footer`/`chakra.div`/`chakra.button` so colours and localeButton interactive states … come from the theme config rather than inline styles".
- `b231f06 refactor(footer): migrate layout to footer.ts theme config` — "Moves all responsive layout CSS out of the inline `FooterStyles` `<style>` tag into `footer.ts` … removing the `!important` injection-order guards."
- `3220239 refactor(zimm-text-input): move colour derivation from the hook into the theme recipe`:
  > "The recipe is the single styling surface for the component, so a variant or state added later cannot disagree with the hook about what colour applies."

**Phase 4 — Folder taxonomy (17, 39).** `39ad495 refactor(ui-kits): organise components into atoms/ and molecules/ subdirectories`, later extended to `organisms/`.

**Phase 5 — Decomposition (~43–45, the ones that produce the final shape).** `theme/components/footer.ts`'s 33 parts split across five co-located `.css.ts` files plus `footerShared.ts`, and the extraction of `ZimmSubscribeSection`/`ZimmSubscribeModal`/`ZimmModal`/`ZimmContactIconRow` out of the footer's inline JSX.

**Phase 6 — Guards, then coverage (30, 31, 36, 42).** `3ba238e test(theme): add recipe guards and text-input colour coverage`:
> "recipeGuards.test.ts covers three failure modes that produce plausible-looking CSS rather than an error, so nothing else would catch them … **Each guard was verified by mutation: reintroducing the defect fails that guard and nothing else.**"

`ec5bf9b test(ui-kit): cover unsafe-href fallback and input-action validation` — "Mutation-verified: removing the `(?!\/)` lookahead fails it, and so does allowing `javascript:`."

**What the sequence reveals about the intended build order:**
1. Build it working and inline first, pixel-matched against Figma with node IDs recorded.
2. Convert every literal to `var(--zimm-*)` at the point of use. Reject any indirection layer over it.
3. Move every interactive state from React state into the recipe.
4. Move every layout rule from inline `<style>`/`style` props into the recipe.
5. Split the monolithic recipe by component ownership, extracting reusable components out of the parent as you go.
6. Only then write the guards — and mutation-verify each one.

# Part 3 — THE PATTERN

## 3.1 Tokens

**Where they're defined.** `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` — Tier 1, UI-Designer owned, listed in `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md:12-24`. Files: `colour.ts`, `fonts.ts`, `typography.ts`, `gridSystem.ts`, `spacing.ts`, `motion.ts`, `sizes.ts`, `zimmTokens.ts`.

**Two-tier colour, alias-by-reference.** `overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts:1-56` — primitives are private module `const`s, the exported semantic tier reads from them:

```ts
// colour.ts:6-16
const grey = { black: 'black', 900: '#191919', 800: '#282828', … };
// colour.ts:45-55
export const colors = {
  grey, ivory, coral, green, orange, red, opacity,
  background: { '01': ivory[100], '02': ivory[200], … '05': grey[900], … },
```

The rule (`overrideStyling.md`, "The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy"): *"Do the same for any new primitive/alias pair you add — two values can't disagree if only one of them is ever typed."*

**`zimmTokens.ts` is the CSS-var registry, fully derived.** `overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts:1-14`:

```ts
// All --zimm-* variables, derived from the other foundation/* files (the actual source
// of truth, ported from the Figma-to-React work) rather than retyped here.
import { colors } from './colour';
import { fontSizes, lineHeights, letterSpacings, fontWeights } from './typography';
import { spacing, borderWidths, focusRingOffsets } from './spacing';
…
export const zimmTokens: Record<string, string> = {
  '--zimm-color-text-default': colors.text.default,       // :47
  '--zimm-focus-ring': `${borderWidths.default} solid ${colors.border.focus}`,  // composite, :66
```

The only literals left are the 7 numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` Handover aliases with no named-scale equivalent (`'--zimm-scale-700': '28px'` etc.) — documented as "not duplicates, just Handover values with nothing to derive them from."

**How they surface as `var(--zimm-*)`.** `overrides/app/theme/zimmTokensGlobal.tsx:16-27` stringifies the registry onto `:root` via a raw Emotion `<Global>` — deliberately *not* Chakra's `styles.global`:

```ts
// zimmTokensGlobal.tsx:7-10
// Deliberately NOT Chakra's styles.global: Chakra's style processor mangles quoted
// font-family values (verified — "'Futura Round', 'Century Gothic', sans-serif"
// collapses to a single family), which would break the --zimm-font-family-* vars.
```

Mounted twice from one definition — `_app-config/index.tsx:159` and `.storybook/preview.tsx` — "so the two mount points cannot drift."

**The usage hierarchy** (`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, "The hierarchy — reach for these in order"):
1. `textStyle` prop for anything textual — never a raw `fontSize`. It is "the one entry in the hierarchy that isn't a colour/spacing token" because there's no `var()` for a composite expansion.
2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` for colour and spacing. Never a bare Chakra/theme key** — `color="text.default"` and `gap="m"` resolve to the *identical* value and are still forbidden. The stated reason is reviewability: *"a `var(--zimm-*)` reference is unambiguous at every call site, where a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct."*
3. The component's own theme config (`<name>.css.ts` or `theme/components/<name>.ts`).
4. `sx` for a one-off Chakra-prop gap.
5. Scoped `.scss` only when `sx` can't express it.

**Only some foundations are registered as Chakra scales,** and this is load-bearing. `overrides/app/theme/index.ts:29-45`:

```ts
// Registered below: borderWidths, breakpoints, colors, fonts, space, textStyles.
// Deliberately NOT registered, because the Zimmermann scale and the Chakra scale
// use the same key names for different values …
//   fontSizes    Chakra md=16px xs=12px 2xs=10px 3xs=7.2px
//                Zimmermann md=24px xs=16px 2xs=14px 3xs=12px  (4 collisions)
//   sizes        Chakra sizes.lg=32rem vs iconSizes.lg=20px
```

This is why `width: 'xl'` is a real bug, not a style nit — it reads Chakra's `sizes.xl` = 36rem. It shipped a 576px contact icon (`zimmContactIconRow.css.ts:11-16` documents the incident inline).

**Units** (`overrideStyling.md` § Units): `rem` for anything that scales with root font-size (WCAG 1.4.4) — type and the named spacing scale. `px` only for hairline geometry that must *not* scale: border widths, focus-ring offsets. `em` only for breakpoints.

### The rule for when a raw literal is acceptable

`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`: **"Never: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file — reach for the token instead."** With a mechanical downgrade path.

`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` (`npm run audit:tokens`, `package.json` scripts) greps `overrides/app/components/**` and `overrides/app/theme/components/**` for `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.scss`, excluding `*.test.ts(x)` and `*.stories.tsx`:

```js
// scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs:58-60
const HEX_RE = /#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\b/g;
const UNIT_RE = /\b\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:rem|em|px)\b/g;
const EXCEPTION_MARKER_RE = /provisional|pending|placeholder|audit-allow/i;
```

**The downgrade rule** (`auditTokenUsage.mjs:20-27`): a match becomes an *acknowledged exception* — printed but not failing — when **the contiguous non-blank block of lines ending at the match** contains `provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder`, or `audit-allow`:

```js
// auditTokenUsage.mjs:119-123
let contextStart = idx;
while (contextStart > 0 && lines[contextStart - 1].trim() !== '') contextStart -= 1;
const context = lines.slice(contextStart, idx + 1).join('\n');
const acknowledged = EXCEPTION_MARKER_RE.test(context);
```

The blank-line boundary (not a fixed N-line window) is deliberate, and the header says why: real exception comments here are multi-line blocks covering several sibling declarations, or wrap the marker across a line break — *"A fixed N-line window missed both shapes during this script's own first calibration pass."*

The header also states the rationale for reusing prose as the allow-list: *"This is the exact vocabulary this codebase already uses for every documented raw-value exception today … Reading the existing explanatory comment as the allow-list entry avoids a second, separately-maintained list that would drift from the code the moment either one changes."*

**What a compliant exception actually looks like** — `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts:3-13`:

```ts
// Provisional spacing/size values — kept here as named references until the UI designer
// confirms the token in foundation/spacing.ts or foundation/sizes.ts.
//
// SPACE_SECTION is NOT a missing token: --zimm-scale-1200 (48px) already carries the same
// value. Kept as rem here because that foundation alias is px, which does not scale under
// browser zoom (WCAG 1.4.4 …). Collapse onto the var once the foundation alias moves to rem.
const SPACE_SECTION = '3rem';        // alias/space/section (48px)
const SIZE_COL_SUB = '20rem';        // alias/size/footer/col-width-subscribe (320px)
const SIZE_COL_MAP = '37.5rem';      // alias/size/footer/col-width-sitemap (600px)
const COLOUR_HALF_INV = 'rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.5)'; // alias/color/opacity-50-inverse
```

Note the shape: **named constant + Figma alias path in a trailing comment + a block comment saying what it's waiting on.** Never an inline literal.

`audit-allow:` is for a *permanent* exception where no token will ever exist — `overrides/app/theme/components/footerShared.ts:15-17`:

```ts
// audit-allow: raw em is correct and permanent here, not a placeholder awaiting a token —
// overrideStyling.md's Units section documents breakpoints as one of the few genuinely
// context-relative uses of em, deliberately outside the var(--zimm-*) scale system.
```

Others: `zimmLogo/index.tsx:9-13` (`// provisional` on `LOGO_MAX_WIDTH`/`LOGO_HEIGHT`, with a `§7 raise:` annotation naming the target foundation file and owner); `zimmTextInput.css.ts:26-38` (`PROVISIONAL pending Kiera`); `zimmSubscribeSection.css.ts:6-12` (`PROVISIONAL: … Pending Kiera`); `zimmNavItem.css.ts:5-11` (`No 4.5px entry exists in spacing.ts — same provisional treatment as zimmButton.css.ts's BTN_PADDING_Y`).

**Two separate enforcement mechanisms, do not confuse them** (`overrideStyling.md` says this explicitly): `recipeGuards.test.ts` runs on every `npm run test` and catches *a bare Chakra key standing in for a zimm var*; `audit:tokens` catches *a raw hex/px/rem/em literal*. Neither is in CI as a hard gate for `audit:tokens` — deliberately, pending triage of 14 pre-existing findings.

---

## 3.2 Component taxonomy — atoms / molecules / organisms

**There is no written definition anywhere.** I grepped `.claude/rules/`, `.claude/skills/`, `.docs/architecture.md`, `README.md`: the words `atoms`/`molecules`/`organisms` appear only as *path fragments in examples*. The taxonomy is defined entirely by the code. That's a real gap worth naming.

Here is the rule the code actually follows:

### Atom — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/<name>/`
`zimmButton`, `zimmIcon`, `zimmLogo`, `zimmModal`, `zimmNavItem`, `zimmTextInput` (+ later `zimmProduct*`)

Distinguishing property: **an atom composes no other Zimmermann component.** Its imports are React, Chakra, and foundation/icons only. It maps props → one DOM/Chakra element (plus its own decorations).

- `zimmNavItem/index.tsx` — imports only `chakra`, `useStyleConfig`, `isSafeHref`. Renders one `<a>` or one `<button>` with a single `<span>` inside.
- `zimmLogo/index.tsx` — one inline `<svg>`. No Chakra recipe at all; it uses `useToken('colors', …)` because "an SVG `fill` attribute needs a concrete colour value, not a custom-property reference" (`:22-23`).
- `zimmIcon/index.tsx` — a switch over 34 icon types from the icons barrel.
- `zimmButton/index.tsx` — imports `ZimmIcon`, which looks like a violation, but it's a *rendering primitive*, not a composed unit; the file describes itself as "a thin mapping layer: Zimmermann props (inverse, large/medium) → Chakra variant/size names that `zimmButton.css.ts` recognises" (`:7-8`).
- `zimmModal/index.tsx` is the most instructive case: it's a portal + backdrop + dialog panel — structurally large, but classified atom because it **owns no content**: *"Generic modal chrome — portal, backdrop, and an accessible dialog panel. Owns none of the content: a caller supplies its own form/fields as children"* (`:26-27`).

**So: atom = single indivisible UI primitive with no Zimmermann-component children and no domain knowledge.** Size and DOM complexity are irrelevant; `zimmModal` is 64 lines and `zimmLogo` is 80, both atoms.

### Molecule — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/<name>/`
`zimmInputAction`, `zimmContactIconRow` (+ later `zimmProductContent`, `zimmProductMeta`)

Distinguishing property: **composes ≥2 atoms (or repeats one) into a single reusable unit, and may own local UI state — but no business/domain state and no data source.**

- `zimmInputAction/index.tsx:3-5` imports `ZimmTextInput`, `ZimmButton`, `ZimmIconType`. It owns `useState<string|undefined>(validationError)` (`:37`) — pure presentation-level validation, no domain meaning. It has **no `.css.ts`** because it adds no styling of its own beyond `__css={{ display: 'block', width: '100%' }}` on the form (`:60`) — the atoms carry the look.
- `zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx` repeats one atom (`ZimmIcon`) three times with per-channel href logic. It *does* have a `.css.ts` because it introduces its own layout (`row` gap/padding, `iconLink` 24px touch target).

### Organism — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/<name>/`
`zimmSubscribeModal`, `zimmSubscribeSection`

Distinguishing property: **composes molecules/atoms AND binds to a hook that owns a state machine or a feature flow.**

- `zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:47-52` — composes `ZimmInputAction` (molecule) + `ZimmSubscribeModal` (organism), calls `useSubscribeSection(...)` returning `{submitState, modalOpen, closeModal, handleEmailSubmit, handleModalSubmit}`, plus `useUiCopy()` for microcopy, plus its own multipart recipe. It renders a four-state discriminated union (`idle`/`success`/`unavailable`/`error`).
- `zimmSubscribeModal/index.tsx` — composes three atoms, calls `useZimmModal({isOpen, onClose})` for focus/scroll/keyboard mechanics, and consumes **two** recipes: `ZimmModal` (chrome, as `chrome`) and `ZimmSubscribeModal` (its own content).

### The extraction test that decides placement
Both organisms and `zimmContactIconRow` state their extraction criterion explicitly in their JSDoc, and it is the same sentence pattern each time — **"nothing here is <parent>-specific":**

> `zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:43-44`: "Extracted from the footer so it can be reused anywhere a storefront needs the same channels — **nothing here is footer-specific.**"

> `zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:30-31`: "**Extracted from the footer so it can be placed on any page**, not just the global footer."

> `zimmModal/index.tsx:28-29`: "Split out of the footer's original SubscribeModal so **any future dialog — not just the subscribe flow** — can reuse the same accessible shell."

By contrast, `FooterNavColumn` and `BottomBar` **stayed in `components/footer/`** as sub-folders, not in `ui-kits/`, precisely because they *are* footer-specific:

> `footerNavColumn/index.tsx:28-31`: "One footer nav column: heading, link list, and (for the Contact group) the contact-channel icon row. Extracted from Footer's inline JSX — **this is where the Figma pixel-precision workarounds below actually live now**, rather than being buried in the footer assembly."

**Governance follows this split:** `CODEOWNERS:176` routes all of `ui-kits/` to *both squads* ("the shared design-system layer consumed by both squads' component overrides"); `CODEOWNERS:87` routes `components/footer/` to both squads + tier-2 + tier-1 approvers.

## 3.3 Focused vs shared styles — **the decision rule**

This is the single most precisely-specified thing in the repo. It's a **four-way decision**, and the first two branches do most of the work.

### The rule

**Step 1 — Does the style belong to a component that could stand alone? Then extract the component, and the style goes into that component's own `<name>.css.ts`.**

This is the primary split, and it's why the footer produced *six* recipes rather than one. `footer.css.ts:15-19` states its own scope boundary as a header comment — this is the pattern's self-documenting form:

```ts
// footer.css.ts owns only the footer's own shell — root container, main layout, the
// subscribe/links content row, and the logo band. Subscribe content, the subscribe modal, nav
// columns, contact icons, and the bottom bar each own their own recipe now — see
// zimmSubscribeSection.css.ts, zimmSubscribeModal.css.ts, footerNavColumn.css.ts,
// zimmContactIconRow.css.ts, bottomBar.css.ts.
```

And the reciprocal boundary, from the generic side — `zimmModal.css.ts:1-4`:

```ts
// Generic dialog chrome — overlay + panel + actions row. Component-specific content styling
// (title, fields, consent copy, etc.) belongs in the consuming organism's own recipe, not here —
// see e.g. zimmSubscribeModal.css.ts. Split out of the footer's original combined recipe so a
// future non-subscribe modal has somewhere to register its own chrome and content separately.
```

**Step 2 — Is the value used by exactly one `.css.ts`? Then it is a module-local `const` in that file.** Even when it's provisional, even when it's a raw literal. `SPACE_SECTION`, `SIZE_COL_SUB`, `SIZE_COL_MAP`, `COLOUR_HALF_INV` (`footer.css.ts:10-13`); `SIZE_SUB_BODY_MAX`, `SIZE_SUBSCRIBE_SLOT` (`zimmSubscribeSection.css.ts:4,12`); `NAV_ITEM_PAD_Y` (`zimmNavItem.css.ts:11`); `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y` (`zimmButton.css.ts:205-207`).

Being provisional is *not* a trigger to share it. `zimmSubscribeSection.css.ts:1-3` makes this explicit — a value that was previously shared got **pulled back down** into the single file that uses it:

```ts
// alias/size/footer/subscribe-body-max (200px). Provisional, pending a foundation/sizes.ts entry.
// Was a named constant in theme/components/footer.ts before the footer decomposition inlined it;
// restored so the value is named at the point of declaration rather than only commented at use.
const SIZE_SUB_BODY_MAX = '12.5rem';
```

**Step 3 — Is the value needed by ≥2 co-located `.css.ts` files *and* must they never diverge? Then, and only then, a small non-recipe constants module in `theme/components/<feature>Shared.ts`.**

`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, "Co-locating a component's theme file":

> "**Cross-file shared values** (a breakpoint or provisional size needed by more than one split-out file) go in a small shared module that stays in `theme/components/` — e.g. `footerShared.ts`, holding the breakpoints and **the one size value** `footerNavColumn.css.ts` and `bottomBar.css.ts` both need. **Don't copy the same literal into two co-located files;** that's exactly the drift risk 'The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy' (above) already warns about."

`footerShared.ts` contains exactly **two** exports, and each one carries its own two-part justification — *who uses it* and *why divergence breaks something*:

```ts
// footerShared.ts:3-7
// Shared between footer's split recipe files (footer.css.ts, footerNavColumn.css.ts,
// bottomBar.css.ts) so a breakpoint or provisional size can't drift between them the way a
// copy-pasted literal would. Not a general-purpose theme module — scope stays footer-only; …
```

```ts
// footerShared.ts:24-28
// alias/size/footer/col-width-nav (140px). Provisional … Used by both the nav column's own width
// (footerNavColumn.css.ts) and the bottom bar's mobile legal-link width (bottomBar.css.ts) — the
// two must match or the legal links stop lining up with the columns above them.
export const SIZE_COL_NAV = '8.75rem';
```

Verify the claim: `footerNavColumn.css.ts:31` uses it as `col.width`; `bottomBar.css.ts:77` uses it as `legalGrid`'s `'& > a': { width: SIZE_COL_NAV }`. Both are consumed and they are visually coupled.

`BP` similarly: `footer.css.ts:43,54,62,65,77,82,85,120`; `footerNavColumn.css.ts:34`; `bottomBar.css.ts:18,38,45,78,84`.

**Step 4 — Is it a genuinely new design token, or app-wide? Then `theme/foundation/` (Tier 1) or a designer-owned `theme/components/<name>.ts`.**

### Three properties of the shared module that make it work

1. **It is not a recipe.** `footerShared.ts` exports plain `const`s and is **not** in `theme/components/index.ts` (`index.ts:1-19` — it isn't there). Chakra never sees it. This keeps "one canonical styling surface per component" intact: the shared module supplies *inputs*, not styles.
2. **It is scope-fenced by name and by comment.** `footerShared`, not `shared`. "Not a general-purpose theme module — scope stays footer-only."
3. **It is the one place that may import from `foundation/` directly.** `footerShared.ts:1` does `import { breakpoints } from '../foundation/gridSystem'` — and `:13-14` justifies it: *"Media queries cannot consume `var()`, so this is the one deliberate exception to `theme/components/` otherwise avoiding direct `foundation/` imports in favour of `--zimm-*` CSS vars."* Note `tablet` is *imported* from the foundation while `tabletWide`/`desktop` are literals — again, reference-not-copy applied at the value level.

### The governance consequence — a second-order part of the rule

Moving a value into `theme/components/` **changes who must approve it.** `CODEOWNERS:178-186`:

```
# ── TIER 3: Component style files (co-located *.css.ts) ────────
# … Placed last among the components/ rules — CODEOWNERS uses last-match-wins, not
# most-specific-wins — so this overrides the heavier Tier 2 directory rules above …
overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts    @ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-a @ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b
```

vs `CODEOWNERS:117` — `overrides/app/theme/components/` → `@ZimmermannAU/tier-2-approvers @ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`.

`overrideStyling.md` states the intent: *"a co-located file is for composing a component's own layout from **already-established** tokens … not for authoring new raw design values."*

And it flags where its own rule has already been violated, without papering over it:

> **"Known inconsistency, flagged not resolved.** … `button.ts` … is now `ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts`, which the `**/*.css.ts` rule above routes to the squads — so those provisional, unapproved constants are **no longer designer-gated**, while still keying the app-wide `Button` recipe. … Whether `zimmButton.css.ts` should be re-gated is an open governance question, not a doc fix, and is deliberately left open here."

### Summary table

| Situation | Goes where | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Style belongs to a self-standing, reusable component | Extract to `ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<name>/<name>.css.ts` | `zimmContactIconRow.css.ts`, `zimmModal.css.ts` |
| Style belongs to a parent-specific sub-part | Sub-folder under the parent: `<parent>/<part>/<part>.css.ts` | `footer/bottomBar/bottomBar.css.ts` |
| Value used by exactly one recipe (even if provisional/raw) | Module-local `const` in that recipe | `footer.css.ts:10-13`, `zimmSubscribeSection.css.ts:4` |
| Value used by ≥2 sibling recipes and must not diverge | `theme/components/<feature>Shared.ts`, constants only, not registered | `footerShared.ts` (BP, SIZE_COL_NAV) |
| New design token, or app-wide | `theme/foundation/` (Tier 1) | `zimmTokens.ts`, `spacing.ts` |
| Recipe for a base-SFCC component being partially overridden | Stays in `theme/components/<name>.ts`, designer-gated | `header.ts`, `listMenu.ts`, `navConstants.ts` |

## 3.4 CSS structure — the `.css.ts` recipe convention

### Naming and location
`<componentFolderName>.css.ts`, in the same directory as the component's `index.tsx`. camelCase for Zimmermann-authored files (`.claude/rules/conventions.md` § File naming).

### Two shapes

**Multipart (the common case)** — a plain object literal with `parts` + `baseStyle`. `footerNavColumn.css.ts:3-5`:

```ts
export const ZimmFooterNavColumn = {
  parts: ['col', 'heading', 'list', 'listItem'],
  baseStyle: { col: {…}, heading: {…}, list: {…}, listItem: {…} },
};
```

**Single-part with variants** — `defineStyleConfig`. `zimmNavItem.css.ts:74-78`:

```ts
export const ZimmNavItem = defineStyleConfig({
  baseStyle,
  variants,                       // { light, inverse }
  defaultProps: { variant: 'light' },
});
```

`zimmButton.css.ts:243` is the same shape with `baseStyle`, `variants` (primary/primaryInverse/secondary/secondaryInverse/icon/iconInverse), `sizes` (lg/sm/icon), `defaultProps`.

**Function-form `baseStyle` for state-driven styling** — `zimmTextInput.css.ts:42-80`:

```ts
/** State the component feeds in so the recipe can resolve the Figma colour cascade. */
export type ZimmTextInputStyleProps = { inverse?: boolean; disabled?: boolean; hasError?: boolean; focused?: boolean; filled?: boolean; };

/** Border colour precedence: disabled > error > focus > filled > default. */
export const resolveBorderColour = ({ inverse, disabled, hasError, focused, filled }: ZimmTextInputStyleProps) => { … };

export const ZimmTextInput = {
  parts: ['root','row','content','label','input','clearButton','helper','error'],
  baseStyle: (props: ZimmTextInputStyleProps): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => { … },
};
```

Note the resolvers are **exported** — so they're unit-testable without asserting on generated CSS (`zimmTextInput.css.test.ts`).

### Export naming — `Zimm*` prefix is mandatory and load-bearing

`overrides/app/theme/index.ts:64` composes with `extendTheme(baseTheme, overrides)`, which **deep-merges**. `recipeGuards.test.ts:18-22`:

> "A recipe key that collides with a base SFCC recipe. `theme/index.ts` composes with `extendTheme(baseTheme, overrides)`, which **DEEP MERGES** — a recipe named `Footer` does not replace SFCC's `Footer`, it inherits it. Shared part names then pick up base properties, and a key you add that the base lacks is appended last, so a CSS shorthand can silently reset a longhand the base declared earlier."

Commit `e950e6e`'s body records the observed symptom: *"Under the old name the copyright rendered at 14px instead of 10px and the subscribe heading lost its 24px gap."*

Guarded by `recipeGuards.test.ts:347-361` with an explicit allow-list: `const INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu'];` — the three where inheriting the base is the point.

### Registration

Every recipe, wherever the file lives, is imported and re-exported from `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`:

```ts
// theme/components/index.ts:1-8
import { Button } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css';
import { ZimmFooter } from 'app/components/footer/footer.css';
import { ZimmFooterNavColumn } from 'app/components/footer/footerNavColumn/footerNavColumn.css';
import { ZimmFooterBottomBar } from 'app/components/footer/bottomBar/bottomBar.css';
…
export const components = { Button, ZimmFooter, ZimmFooterNavColumn, … };
```

> "Chakra resolves a recipe by the string key passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path, so co-location is purely an organisational choice with no runtime difference." — `overrideStyling.md`

### Binding to the component

The recipe key is a named constant at the top of `index.tsx`, never inline:

```ts
// footer/index.tsx:15
const ZIMM_FOOTER_RECIPE = 'ZimmFooter';
// footer/index.tsx:88
const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_FOOTER_RECIPE, {});
// footer/index.tsx:91-93
<chakra.footer role="contentinfo" __css={styles.container}>
  <chakra.div __css={styles.main}>
    <chakra.div __css={styles.contentRow}>
```

Single-part: `const styles = useStyleConfig('ZimmNavItem', { variant });` → `__css={styles}` (`zimmNavItem/index.tsx:33,41`).

Two recipes in one component: `zimmSubscribeModal/index.tsx:37-38` binds `chrome` (ZimmModal) and `styles` (its own).

Markup is `chakra.*` elements (`chakra.footer`, `chakra.div`, `chakra.button`, `chakra.ul`, `chakra.li`, `chakra.p`, `chakra.a`, `chakra.span`, `chakra.form`) — so `__css` accepts the resolved recipe part.

Per-instance deviations merge over the part, never replace it:
```ts
// footerNavColumn/index.tsx:42-45
__css={{ ...styles.heading, ...(group.fields.showContactChannels ? { paddingLeft: 'var(--zimm-scale-2xs)' } : {}) }}
```

### Responsive steps are explicit media queries, never Chakra's array shorthand

```ts
// footer.css.ts:43-48
[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: {
  flexDirection: 'row',
  justifyContent: 'space-between',
  gap: 0,
  padding: `var(--zimm-scale-4xl) var(--zimm-scale-3xl) ${SPACE_SECTION}`,
},
```

The reason (`overrideStyling.md`): *"The array shorthand (`['2xs','2xs','xs','xs']`) … would put a bare token key back at every step — the guard walks responsive arrays and attributes each element to the same prop, so all four fail. `footer.css.ts`'s `contentRow` and `linksInner` parts are the reference."*

### The "one canonical styling surface" rule

From `overrideStyling.md`:

> "Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its theme config … Don't also give it a `.zimm-*` global class in `globalStyles.ts` — a static CSS class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/`_focusVisible` states the way a Chakra theme config can, so a class 'mirror' is **structurally incomplete from the start**, and nothing stops its values from disagreeing with the real theme config over time."

The rule extends past global classes to **React state and hooks**. Two commits enforce it:
- `dc86c13` — deleted `useState` for hovered/pressed/focused from `ZimmButton`; `index.tsx:37-38` now says "All visual states are handled by `zimmButton.css.ts` … no React state for hover/press/focus."
- `3220239` — moved colour derivation out of `useZimmTextInputState` into `zimmTextInput.css.ts`: *"The recipe is the single styling surface for the component, so a variant or state added later cannot disagree with the hook about what colour applies."* The hook now returns only interaction state.

`.zimm-*` classes remain valid only for "genuinely static, non-interactive, massively-reused treatments (typography, the responsive grid, form-field layout)."

### Comment density is part of the convention

Every non-obvious declaration carries the Figma node ID, the measurement, the alternative that was tried, and the outcome. `footerNavColumn.css.ts:6-25` is the canonical example — 20 lines of comment for a 13-line `col` part, including a measured table:

```
//   ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF COUNTRY  212 / ~188  -> wraps under both            (> 160)
//   "ACKNOWLEDGEMENT" alone     130 / ~115  -> break lands after it        (< 160)
//   BOOK AN APPOINTMENT         149 / ~135  -> stays on one line under both (< 160)
// A 140px cap (SIZE_COL_NAV) was tried first and wrongly wrapped BOOK AN APPOINTMENT.
```

And `bottomBar.css.ts:22-25` records a bug's root cause at the site of the fix:
```
// Gutter widens here, not at BP.desktop. footer.css.ts's contentRow and logo both step
// from 2xl to 3xl at BP.tablet, so holding this at 2xl until 1024px left the whole
// 768-1023px band with the bottom bar inset 8px less than the content above it …
```

## 3.5 Override approach

**Mechanism.** `package.json`'s `ccExtensibility: { "extends": "@salesforce/retail-react-app", "overridesDir": "overrides" }`. A file at `overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx` intercepts every `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/footer` import — including the base template's own internal ones.

**Override vs custom, by filename.** `.claude/rules/conventions.md` § File naming:
- **Override** (mirrors a base Salesforce file): keep the original kebab-case name and folder exactly — `product-tile/`, `_app-config/`, `footer/`, `header/`. "This makes the origin of a file obvious at a glance."
- **Custom** (Zimmermann-authored): camelCase — `footerNavColumn/`, `uiCopyProvider/`, `zimmNavItem/`, `useZimmModal.ts`.
- Both are `.ts`/`.tsx` always (AGENTS.md's strict rule).

**Copy-first porting** (AGENTS.md § Rules, "Copy-first rule") — four steps, then a mandatory stop:
1. Copy each base file from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/`.
2. Convert to TypeScript and update imports.
3. `npx tsc --noEmit`.
4. Add a temporary `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')` to each, **stop, and let the user verify the override is rendering** before any functional change. Remove the logs once confirmed.

The footer PR shows the long-tail consequence. `header/index.tsx` was copy-first ported earlier; PR #59's entire diff there is **comments only** (+24/−0), explaining the dead imports left behind by the port:

```tsx
// header/index.tsx (added in PR #59)
// AccountIcon and HeartIcon are imported but not rendered. They serve the commented-out
// base SFCC icon-button block further down this file … That block was disabled when this
// file was first copied into overrides/ per the copy-first rule, and is superseded by the
// Account | Saved | Bag *text* buttons the Zimmermann header design uses instead …
// Kept as a reference to the base implementation, per AGENTS.md's rule on commented-out code.
```

Commit `77042f8 docs(header): explain the disabled base SFCC icon-button block` — "Comments only — no functional change." This is the pattern's answer to dead code inherited from a port: **explain it in place, don't delete it** (AGENTS.md: "Do not remove existing commented-out code or comments").

**What an override actually intercepts — the seam.** `footer/index.tsx:158-171` documents it precisely:

> "The component SFCC actually renders. Base `_app/index.jsx` resolves `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/footer` through the overrides system and renders `<Footer />` with **no props**, so there is no upstream container to own the data. This wrapper is that seam, and the only place the Contentful fetch lives."

Hence the file has **two exports**: a named `Footer` (presentational, `data` required, fetches nothing) and a default `FooterContainer` (the interception point that supplies data). This is the general shape — the default export must satisfy the base's calling convention; the named export is what stories, tests and other Zimmermann code consume.

**The import-path trap.** `overrideStyling.md`, "Importing an already-overridden component from a new component":

> "If component A uses component B, and B already has an override, **import B via a relative path (`'../swatch-group'`), not the SFCC base path** … The resolver that redirects `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` (`ccExtensibility` … read by a webpack plugin) only runs in the **real app build**. `.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to `node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it at all … A base-path import of an already-overridden component will build and run correctly in the shipped app, but silently render/test the **unstyled base SFCC version** in Storybook and Vitest."

A live instance is named and left open: `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice` import.

**The SFCC bridge pattern** (for components SFCC's own base code imports internally): the default export stays a faithful, undecorated port with the full original prop surface and `forwardRef` behaviour; Zimmermann-only styling goes behind a named export (`product-tile`'s `CardBaseline`) or, preferably now, a theme recipe.

**Tier discipline is part of the mechanism, not around it.** Every commit touching a Tier 1 path states the file, the tier, and the verified identity in the commit body (`b1d137a`, `34486eb`, `2381909`). `b1d137a style(theme): drop the stray trailing newline in foundation/sizes.ts` is the extreme case — a whitespace-only Tier 1 commit that exists so the branch's diff against `develop` for that file is *empty*: "Whitespace only. No token, scale or value is touched."

## 3.6 Contentful

PR #59 is where Contentful wiring is established, and its rule is: **components never fetch; the content type, the TypeScript type, and the fixture are authored together.**

**Content model authoring.** Moved in this PR from per-environment migrations to one org-scoped Environment Template. Deleted: `scripts/contentful/sync.js`, `setup/runMigrations.mjs`, `setup/detectDrift.mjs`, `migrations/001-initial-content-types.mjs`. Added: `scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js` (+166), `setup/installTemplate.mjs` (+199), `setup/seedRegions.mjs` (+93), and one file per content type in `scripts/contentful/content-types/`: `footerConfig.js`, `footerNavGroup.js`, `link.js`, `region.js`, `uiCopy.js`. These are Tier 2, Integration-owned (`protectedFiles.md` § Contentful Schema Definitions): *"`content-types/*.js` is the sole source of truth per content type (including `localized`/`required`/`validations`)."*

The definition carries the same explanatory-comment discipline as the recipes — `scripts/contentful/content-types/footerConfig.js:31-34`:

```js
// Contact channels rendered by ContactIconRow. Optional: a storefront without a
// channel renders that icon non-interactive rather than hiding the row. Values are
// passed through isSafeHref before reaching an anchor, so an editor cannot introduce
// a javascript:/data: URL from the CMS.
{ id: 'phoneHref', name: 'Phone Href', type: 'Symbol', required: false, localized: false },
```

**The TypeScript mirror.** `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts:86-148` declares `LinkEntry`, `FooterNavGroupEntry`, `FooterConfigEntry` to the exact nested shape `include: 3` produces, with a header pointing at the authoring files (`:81-83`). Arrays are `ReadonlyArray<>` **and** `readonly`, with the reason stated (`:135-141`): the fixture is a module singleton read by several stories, so an in-place mutation anywhere would corrupt the others.

**Schema/type/component are changed as one unit.** The CodeRabbit finding — "`FooterConfigEntry` … declares `phoneHref`, `whatsAppHref`, and `emailHref` … This schema declares none of them" — was resolved by adding the three fields to the content type, the TS type, and the component call site in one commit, and the resolution reply names all three.

**The English-string bug and its fix are the canonical Contentful lesson.** CodeRabbit: *"Do not key layout behaviour off the English heading text. … The heading is localised Contentful content, and this footer ships to eight storefronts. For any locale whose heading is not exactly 'Contact', … the phone, WhatsApp, and email channels disappear."* Resolution: a `showContactChannels?: boolean` field on `footerNavGroup`, documented on the type itself (`types/contentful.ts:110-116`):

```ts
/**
 * Renders the contact-channel icon row beneath this group's links.
 *
 * A flag rather than matching the heading text: `heading` is a localised Contentful
 * value, so `heading === 'Contact'` silently stops matching the moment an editor writes
 * "Kontakt" or "Contacto" — and this footer ships to eight storefronts.
 */
showContactChannels?: boolean;
```

**Region scoping is a shared utility, not per-component logic.** `overrides/app/utils/resolveByRegion.ts` exports `filterByRegion` and `pickMostSpecificByRegion`; `footer/index.tsx:144-156` exports a pure, testable `scopeToRegion(config, siteId)` that uses them. Omitted/empty `regions` = the global default; a narrower entry wins.

**Fetch depth is a named constant with a failure analysis** — `footer/index.tsx:17-27`:

```ts
// Contentful resolves nested references `include` levels deep, and the footer model is exactly
// three: footerConfig → navGroups (1) → links (2) → regions (3). …
// Getting this wrong fails hard, not gracefully. At 2, a region-scoped link's `regions` array
// arrives as unresolved link stubs with no `fields` … the `.catch` below swallows it,
// footerData stays null and the *entire* footer renders nothing …
const FOOTER_INCLUDE_DEPTH = 3;
```

**No fallback content on failure** (`:166-169`): "Renders nothing while loading, on fetch failure, or when no entry resolves for this region — no fallback to placeholder content once wired to live data, so a Contentful outage doesn't silently ship stale placeholder copy to real shoppers."

**Fixtures are Storybook-only, by construction.** At PR-review time CodeRabbit flagged `FOOTER_FIXTURE` reaching the production path ("All production data must come from the live Commerce Cloud API … do not use MSW or hardcoded fixtures in production paths"). The resolution moved the fixture to `footer/index.stories.content.ts`, whose docblock is the rule:

> "Storybook-only fixture for `index.stories.tsx`, shaped exactly like a resolved Contentful CDA response for the `footerConfig` content type. FooterContainer (index.tsx's default export) fetches real content instead — this fixture only ever feeds the presentational `Footer` export directly, so stories render offline without a live CMS connection, per components.md's Contentful story-mocking rule."

**Contentful Studio Experiences component registration is a separate concern** — there's a dedicated `contentful-register-component` skill and `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts`. PR #59 *removed* the shoppable-image experience components; the footer is **not** registered as a Studio component. So: content-type-backed ≠ Studio-registered, and the footer is the former only.

**Microcopy is a third channel**, distinct from both props and Contentful business data. `useUiCopy()` reads a Provider mounted in `_app-config`, degrades to English literals with no Provider, and is the one documented exception to the no-data-fetching-in-components rule (`.claude/rules/components.md`, added in this PR).

## 3.7 Stories and tests — what every component must ship

### Story: required, one per exported component

`.claude/rules/components.md` § Storybook: required for anything another file imports; not required for purely internal sub-components.

**Uniform imports** (a CodeRabbit finding in this PR standardised them):
```tsx
import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-webpack5';   // framework-specific, NOT '@storybook/react'
import { expect, fn, userEvent, within } from 'storybook/test';     // Storybook re-export, not @testing-library
```

**Title = sidebar category**, from `components.md`'s fixed table. Observed:
- atoms/molecules → `Elements/ZimmNavItem`, `Elements/ZimmButton`, `Elements/ZimmContactIconRow`
- form assemblies → `Forms/ZimmSubscribeSection`, `Forms/ZimmInputAction`
- global chrome → `Layout/Footer`

**Content:** a `Default` export always; named exports for meaningful states, not every prop combination. `zimmButton/index.stories.tsx` has 17 (Default, PrimaryMedium, PrimaryDisabled, PrimaryInverse, PrimaryFullWidth, Secondary…, Icon…, Bag, Close, Menu). `footer/index.stories.tsx` has 6 (Default, Subscribed, SubscribeSubmit, SubscribeModalOpen, ContactChannelFallbacks, SubscribePlaceholder).

**Dark-surface decorator** for inverse variants — `zimmNavItem/index.stories.tsx:21-27`:
```tsx
const darkDecorator = [(Story: React.ComponentType) => (
  <Box bg="background.05" p={4} display="inline-flex"><Story /></Box>
)];
```

**`play` is required when there is interactive behaviour worth asserting** — validation, disclosure, focus management, controlled input. The PR's Testing block reports "15 `play` functions across 7 stories." Queries go through `within(canvasElement)`, `getByRole` with an accessible name first. CodeRabbit enforced both rules on this PR ("Keep Storybook interaction queries inside the story canvas", "Fix footer stories `getByRole` selector to use accessible name `{name:/email/i}`").

**Stories are used as security/behaviour proof, not just visuals.** `zimmNavItem`'s `PlaceholderButton` story renders all four unsafe-href rejection cases (omitted, `javascript:`, `data:`, `//example.com`) and asserts each falls back to `<button>` with no href — commit `ec5bf9b` notes it is "Mutation-verified: removing the `(?!\/)` lookahead fails it, and so does allowing `javascript:`." Both sides of a boolean flag get their own story: `Filled` (no clear control, the default) and `Clearable` (`2dd5e13`).

Storybook `play` runs in CI via `qa.yml`'s `storybook-test` job on `overrides/app/components/**`.

### Tests

**The rule PR #59 added to `.claude/rules/testing.md`** (the paragraph is new in this PR):

> "**This is not license to skip a component's own test file because its behaviour happens to be covered transitively elsewhere.** A component with real logic (branching, prop→JSX mapping decisions, event wiring) gets its own `index.test.ts(x)` … Resolve the duplication concern by **scoping what that file asserts** — mock the hook/child component whose internals are proven elsewhere, and test only this component's own contract … A component with no branching or decision logic at all (pure prop interpolation, e.g. `BottomBar`) still doesn't need its own suite."

So the shipped test artefacts are *selective and justified*, not uniform:

| File | Has test? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `footer/index.test.tsx` (221) | ✅ | container: fetch, region scoping, error branches |
| `footer/footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx` (89) | ✅ | branching on `showContactChannels`, `hasIntentionalLineBreak` |
| `footer/bottomBar/` | ❌ | "pure prop interpolation" — named in the rule as the exemption |
| `ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` (201) | ✅ | named in the rule as the reference pattern |
| `ui-kits/atoms/zimmTextInput/zimmTextInput.css.test.ts` (105) | ✅ | tests the **recipe**, not the component |
| every hook | ✅ | `useSubscribeSection`, `useZimmModal`, `useUiCopy`, `useZimmTextInputState` |
| every util | ✅ | `safeHref.test.ts` (13 cases), `resolveByRegion.test.ts` |

**A recipe can have its own test file** — `zimmTextInput.css.test.ts` imports the exported resolvers directly:
```ts
import { resolveBorderColour, resolveHoverBorderColour, resolveLabelColour, ZimmTextInput } from './zimmTextInput.css';
```
with the reasoning at `:5-9`: *"The Figma colour cascade is the part of this recipe that can break without surfacing as a type or build error — a mis-ordered branch renders a plausible-but-wrong border. These assertions moved here from `useZimmTextInputState.test.ts` when the derivation moved out of the hook and into the theme."*

**Conventions enforced by CodeRabbit on this PR:** `beforeEach` setup + `afterEach(() => vi.clearAllMocks())` in every Vitest file. `zimmTextInput.css.test.ts:11-14` even keeps them where they're inert, and says so: *"The resolvers here are pure and this file mocks nothing, so these hooks are a convention baseline rather than load-bearing isolation — kept so the file matches the rule as written."*

**A known environment gap, documented in the rule with a prescribed workaround** (added by this PR to `testing.md`): `ZimmIcon` throws under Vitest because the base SFCC icons barrel has a top-level side effect. Not fixable from a test file (`vitest.config.ts` is Tier 1). Prescribed mock, used identically in `footer/index.test.tsx:11-14` and `footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx`:
```ts
vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', () => ({ ZimmIcon: () => null }));
```

### Two structural guard suites — the pattern's own safety net

**`overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` (365 lines, new in PR #59).** Guards four silent-failure modes plus one house-style rule, walking the *registered recipe map*:
1. spacing key on a sizing prop (`width: 'xl'` → 576px)
2. bare key on a typography prop (`fontSize: '2xs'` → Chakra's 10px, not Zimmermann's 14px)
3. bare key in a compound shorthand (`padding: 'xs 0'` — Chakra resolves a token only as the *entire* value; the browser drops the declaration)
4. `no recipe silently inherits a base SFCC recipe of the same name` — the `Zimm*` namespacing guard
5. `no override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale` — the house-style guard

Two engineering details worth copying:
- **Exhaustive prop-combination resolution** for function-form `baseStyle`s (`:236-244`): `2^n` combinations, because "`'3xs'` shipped exactly this way: `floated` is false under the all-default combo, so the guard below never saw the string it was meant to catch. Exhaustive, not sampled."
- **A vacuity guard** (`:288-295`): `test('collect() actually walks the registered recipes')`, because "Every other test here asserts an empty offender list, which an empty input satisfies just as well as a clean one."

Its **SCOPE note** is honest about the blind spot: it walks recipes only, so it cannot see the same mistake as a JSX/`sx` prop; a live instance at `header/index.tsx:302` (`fontSize="l"`) is named and left for an ast-grep rule.

**`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts`** (added *after* PR #59, but part of the pattern now): reconciles every `.css.ts`'s declared `parts` against the `styles.<part>` reads in the sibling `index.tsx`. Its header corrects a common misconception with a direct probe result: `parts` does **not** gate `baseStyle` — it gates `variants`/`sizes`, so an undeclared part renders correctly today and silently stops responding to variants the day someone adds one.

### The commit-level test discipline

Guards are **mutation-verified**, and the commit says so. `3ba238e`: *"Each guard was verified by mutation: reintroducing the defect fails that guard and nothing else."* `ec5bf9b`: *"Mutation-verified against three defects: dropping either guard, and the silent-submit case where the error renders but onSubmit fires anyway."*

## 3.8 Loose ends worth knowing before you use this as a template

- **`.claude/rules/overrides.md` does not exist.** `overrideStyling.md` cross-references it four times (`ls .claude/rules/` returns 11 files, not including it). Broken reference.
- **The atom/molecule/organism taxonomy is undocumented.** It exists only as folder structure + the "nothing here is footer-specific" extraction test in JSDoc. Nothing in `.claude/rules/` defines it.
- **`audit:tokens` is not in CI**, deliberately — 14 pre-existing violations need triage first. `overrideStyling.md` calls wiring it as a required check on `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` "the remaining near-term follow-up, not an optional nice-to-have."
- **`zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional constants lost their designer gate** when `button.ts` moved to co-location. Flagged in `overrideStyling.md` as an open governance question, not fixed.
- **The recipe guards can't see JSX/`sx` props.** Two live instances are named in the source: `header/index.tsx:302`'s `fontSize="l"`, and a `paddingLeft: '2xs'` that was found only by manual grep.
- `theme/components/header.ts` is the only multipart recipe not sitting beside its component, so `recipeParts.test.ts` cannot reach it — it's unguarded, and says so.
